children.value: > Fact From Story In his speech Wednesday, Trump tried to play up the division, heaping blame on Biden and the Democrats for the uncertainty around EVs.

> > Fact From Story “If you want to buy an electric car, that’s absolutely fine. I’m all for it. But we should not be forcing consumers to buy electric vehicles they don’t want to buy.” | Fact From Story
> > > Fact From Story “The auto industry is being assassinated,” Trump said, according to Detroit News.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge Saying something is being "assassinated" is an appeal to emotion and concern.

> > > Commonsense Knowledge Politicians often make statements supporting individual choice while simultaneously criticizing policies they oppose. | Commonsense Knowledge
> > Commonsense Knowledge Politicians often blame their opponents for problems in order to gain support. | Commonsense Knowledge
> Fact From Story President Joe Biden has made EVs a major part of his environmental legacy, and Trump senses that the issue could be used to leach support from working-class voters.
> Commonsense Knowledge Politicians often try to create divisions between groups of people in order to gain support.
